comment: Known compliance failures tracked as EXPECTED (not bugs in the shim). Each entry must match exactly; any drift (different query, different diff shape, or allowlist entry that no longer matches anything) fails reconciliation so regressions surface.

tolerances.reason: ClickHouse native modulo uses x - trunc(x / y) * y instead of Go/Prometheus math.Mod, which causes tiny float drift on large operands. Accept only when the rerun against both APIs stays within a 1e-6 absolute margin and labels/timestamps still match exactly.

entries.reason: Prom 3.x added UTF-8 label-name support, so '~invalid' is now a valid destination label and the query succeeds. promshim still validates against the pre-3.x label-name regex (bad_data: invalid destination label name). Matches a class of queries that should only pass once promshim implements UTF-8 label handling. See harness/compliance/scripts/patch-queries-for-prom3.py for why this entry is no longer should_fail upstream.
Same UTF-8 label-name gap as promshim-utf8-label-names-label-replace, but via label_join's destination label argument.

Prometheus topk's tie-break is a storage-layer implementation detail. promql/engine.go:1052 calls querier.Select with sortSeries=false, so the TSDB SeriesSet is iterated in its native postings order (essentially series-ref / scrape-discovery order). aggregationK (engine.go:3776) then iterates 'for si := range inputMatrix' preserving that order, and the heap replacement at engine.go:3865 uses a strict '<' comparison (group.heap[0].F < s.F), so on an exact tie the new element does NOT displace the heap root — first-seen wins. That first-seen order is not derivable from labels alone (labels.Hash / labels.StableHash give alphabetical order; the fixture's TSDB order differs). Reproducing Prom's tie-break exactly would require mirroring its storage layer. On this fixture, demo_memory_usage_bytes series across instance demo.promlabs.com:10000/10001/10002 occasionally hit the same float value (173015040) at the same timestep; Prom and the shim disagree on which instance survives the cut. Affects only exact-value ties, which are rare in real data. Verified against prometheus@57821524d. See harness/compliance/README.md section 'topk tie-break ordering'.
